small_guidance:
- Add larger tile configs (BLOCK_M=128/BLOCK_N=256/BLOCK_K=64 num_warps=8 stages=3-4, and BLOCK_M=256/BLOCK_N=128/BLOCK_K=32) since M=1024,N=8192,K=8192 is large and benefits from bigger tiles; also try num_stages=4 for the long K-loop to overlap loads.
- Add a GROUP_M block-swizzle (e.g. 8) over the (pid_m, pid_n) grid for L2 reuse across N tiles of a row group — current naive 2D grid leaves L2 on the table.
- Pre-transpose W once in __init__ to a contiguous (K, N) buffer so the inner B load is a unit-stride row read instead of strided over stride_wn; this typically yields 10-20% on K=8192.
large_guidance:
- Replace the row-major GEMM with a split-K or persistent-tile GEMM: with K=8192 and only M=1024, the M dimension only fills 8-16 tiles, so persistence + L2-aware swizzle (or split-K with atomic add for the bias/BN/swish epilogue applied after reduction) would better saturate the SMs.
- Consider casting weights/activations to TF32 (`tl.dot(..., allow_tf32=True)` or input cast) — fp32 GEMM on a 4090 is far below peak; TF32 keeps the 5e-2 tolerance and roughly doubles throughput.
- Keep the BN-fold (scale/shift) precomputation in __init__ (cached, not recomputed each forward) so eval-mode forward avoids the rsqrt/mul/sub on every call; only refresh when running stats change.
